text:
Erin: Hey folks, looking for soundtracks that work for low-key late night debugging  Not lo-fi playlists  more like unobtrusive film scores or ambient albums. Any hidden gems?

Sam: Oh nice. 'The Assassin' soundtrack (Hildur J) is subtle and hypnotic, not bombastic.

Devon: For something a little folksy but cinematic, try Nick Drake's 'Pink Moon'  it's tiny and filmic.

Priya: If you want synth noir without the Blade Runner clichés: try Lustmord's quieter tracks or Zola Jesus's instrumental stuff.

ryan: Random rec: 'Only Lovers Left Alive' soundtrack by Jozef van Wissem & Jim Jarmusch  perfect low tempo.

Erin: Love these. Any recommendations for instrumental indie artists?

Sam: Floating Points has a few long instrumental pieces that are great for focus. Also check 'Motion Sickness of Time Travel' OST (small runs, really rare).

Devon: Suggestion: 'Tangerine Dream' early albums  very analog nocturnal vibes, but yes, depends on whether you want melodic.

Priya: Also tagging a shoutout to female composers: Olivia Block, Ellen Fullman, and Annea Lockwood have interesting ambient work.

spotify-bot: Created playlist 'Midnight Scores @Redwood' with 28 tracks from this thread  https://open.spotify.com/playlist/1ExampleBotLink

Erin: haha thanks bot. Quick poll: react with 🎶 for soundtrack, 🎧 for synth, 📚 for book rec that reads like a film.

Sam: 🎶

Devon: 🎧

Priya: 📚 (rec: 'Never Let Me Go'  very cinematic melancholy)

ryan: Also, if anyone's into obscure score composers, try Daniel Hart (collab with indie films).

Erin: This is perfect, I'm adding these now. If someone has vinyl pressings of obscure OSTs I'm jealous 

Sam: I actually have a worn Tangerine Dream LP  will bring it to the office social later.

Devon: Nice  also, tiny shoutout: if the playlist needs pacing I can make a 45-min 'focus set' export (no vocals).

Erin: Please do that Devon, with track timestamps if possible.

Devon: Will post M3U and timestamps by EOD.

Priya: Thanks all, this will make tonight's deploy watchlist much more delightful. :coffee:

Erin: Appreciate it!
